en: The Scripture on Protecting One’s Body and Life Spoken by the Buddha, one fascicle.
Translated by the Monk Daozhen during the Northern Wei dynasty.
This scripture spoken by the Buddha provides protection for those suffering from illness and calamity.
At that time, when the Buddha was between the twin śāla trees, on the verge of parinirvāṇa,
Śāriputra, Ānanda, and immeasurable, boundless great bodhisattvas and great disciples, as well as all the devas, had gathered together.
The Buddha returned to his proper seat and addressed Ānanda, saying:
"I shall now enter parinirvāṇa.
After my parinirvāṇa, within this world of the five turbidities and evil age..."
All sentient beings shall be harassed by evil Māras and malevolent ghosts—
those who suck away the vital essence of humans, those who seek out others' faults, and those who come unprovoked to kill.
Ānanda, you must diligently propagate this sutra.
May all sentient beings in this degenerate age be free from the suffering of illness and untimely death;
may all malevolent influences, sorcery, and poisons be utterly extinguished.
Ānanda, that which I have entrusted to you for the sake of its dissemination is none other than this sutra.
If there should be a gathering of people, whether male or female,
who are able to read and recite even a single line or a single verse of this sutra.
No malevolent spirits or demons shall dare to approach them.
Whether they are in the midst of a wilderness or in the midst of urgent distress, [they shall be protected].
Whether amidst a great conflagration or a vast body of water,
one should always read and recite this sutra;
it can completely eliminate and sever [all such calamities].
Why is this? Because this sutra possesses great majestic power, one should constantly read it.
If one is unable to read it, [one should listen to it].
One should simply write it down, place it within one's breast, and receive and uphold it with a sincere mind.
This sutra sustains the spiritual power of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
If you wish to travel afar, you should always carry it with you.
No wicked beasts or poisonous creatures will be able to approach them.
Wherever they go, whether to villages or elsewhere,
they should single-mindedly expound the Dharma for others whenever there is a need to do so.
Those who listen shall obtain all their aspirations.
Ānanda, the Buddha does not speak falsely.
This sutra is a secret essence of the Buddha’s teaching, most difficult to encounter.
It is like a wondrous medicine that can cure diseases caused by poison and ward off poisonous vapors.
It can sever evil poisons.
Should someone lead a practitioner away,
and various evil venomous insects and manifold malevolent spells and poisons intend to come and inflict harm upon them, [this mantra shall protect them].
Upon smelling the fragrance of this medicine, they dispersed in the four directions, not daring to look back;
this sutra is likewise so.
If there are those who suffer from illness, [they shall be cured].
One should bathe and purify oneself, then recite this with single-minded devotion;
all afflictions will be eliminated.
Thus spoke the Buddha to Ānanda.
If there are evil Māras or various malevolent poisons that do not comply with my words,
I shall cause these Māras to encounter those very same malevolent poisons;
like oil being pressed out of a seed, they shall all be utterly extinguished without remainder.
The Buddha then enumerated the names of the seven Buddhas:
first, Vipaśyin Buddha;
second, Śikhin Buddha.
The third was the Buddha Śiṣyaka;
the fourth was the Buddha Krakucchanda;
the fifth was the Buddha Kanakamuni.
The sixth was Kāśyapa Buddha;
the seventh was Śākyamuni Buddha.
Should there be anyone afflicted by suffering, calamity, illness, or pain, [they shall be delivered].
One should then recite the names of these seven Buddhas;
all evil spells and poisons will be completely extinguished, and none shall be able to approach or harm them.
After the Buddha had spoken this sutra,
Again he addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Out of my compassion for sentient beings once more,
I shall now further explain the names of the six spirits."
The first is named Panara;
the second is named Kanara;
the third is named Canda-ka.
The fourth is named Kinka;
the fifth is named Mathu;
the sixth is named Maki.
These are the names of the six deities.
Ānanda, if there are sentient beings—
whether male or female, noble or lowly— who are beset by suffering and calamity, [they should recite these names].
All should recite the names of the Six Deities;
thus, their ailments will be eliminated,
and malevolent spirits and oppressive energies shall not be able to approach them.
Everything was extinguished and ceased without remainder.
The Buddha addressed the immeasurable and boundless great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, as well as the celestial kings, all devas, humans, and others.
After my parinirvāṇa,
if there are those who receive and uphold the Dharma entrusted by me,
you all should constantly protect them day and night, ensuring they attain peace and security.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, after the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha,
I shall lead twenty-five bodhisattvas."
In this evil age, wherever there may be a place where this sutra is read or recited,
we shall protect that person day and night by remaining at their side;
no malevolent spirits or demons shall be able to approach them.
May this person always be at peace both while sleeping and while awake,
and practice wholesome dharmas.
The Buddha praised Mañjuśrī and the others.
Excellent, excellent!
You are able to protect my resolve for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, which I have cultivated and accumulated throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas.
At that time, the four celestial kings bared their right shoulders, placed their right knees upon the ground,
and with single-minded palms joined, addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, we shall constantly [protect]..."
Each shall lead their retinues to patrol the borders of the kingdom.
Should there be anyone who can read, recite, copy, or uphold this sutra,
we and our retinues will constantly follow that person.
I shall protect them day and night so that they do not encounter evil.
Should this person wish to travel through a wilderness,
I will constantly follow that person, leading and escorting them from the front.
With a diligent mind, they shall protect them and never leave their side,
ensuring that no evil Māras may come to harass or approach them.
They shall always obtain sufficiency, so that they never suffer from hunger or thirst, nor lack anything whatsoever.
Whatever you may desire, we, the divine kings, shall provide it all for you;
there shall be nothing lacking according to your wishes. Why is this?
Because this person is able to disseminate this sutra,
and because they practice wholesome dharmas to make offerings to the Triple Gem,
they shall not allow [the Dharma] to be severed.
At that time, the gandharva kings, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others,
each knelt on one knee before the Tathāgata.
With single-minded devotion, they joined their palms and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, we devas and humans shall always travel through the air; whenever there are those in this evil age who read, recite, copy, or uphold this sutra, [we shall protect them]."
We, the devas and humans, together with our retinues, shall go to the place where this person dwells.
We shall listen to and receive this sutra-dharma,
and we shall constantly provide protection day and night, never departing from the four directions surrounding them.
I shall protect this person;
no māras or evil spirits shall be able to approach them,
nor shall they be able to seize their vital essence.
May no untimely death come upon you.
May no harm or affliction come upon you.
May no one seek to find fault in you.
They shall not be able to commit transgressions,
nor shall their poisonous influence prevail.
We, along with our retinues, will constantly come to the place where this person dwells.
While I am in the air,
if this person should encounter a great fire, we,
along with our retinues, will employ every skillful means to protect their body so that it is not burned by the flames.
If they encounter a great flood and flee in haste, we,
their kinsmen, will immediately come from the air to receive that person.
It shall cause them not to be seen drowning;
they will immediately return and be able to cross over the peril of the waters.
If they encounter great bandits, [it shall likewise protect them].
I shall protect this person from all four directions,
enabling them to inspire thoughts of compassion in the hearts of their enemies so that they will not raise their swords or staves;
and should they encounter the punishments of the law, being bound by fetters and shackles, suffering in grief day and night.
We and our retinues, remaining in the midst of the sky,
shall cause the hearts of those officials to rejoice, so that they will release them all and grant them liberation.
We and our retinues shall protect them with a single-minded resolve.
They shall not allow others to cause them disturbance;
throughout immeasurable and boundless eons,
they shall constantly keep this sutra in mind.
Why is this? Because this sutra is the Dharma with which the World-Honored One has earnestly charged us,
so that it may circulate for a long time.
The Buddha again praised the devas, humans, and others:
"Excellent, excellent!
You and your retinues have, throughout incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*), [practiced virtue]."
They shall encounter hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas,
and furthermore, they shall be able to protect my disciples throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas,
enabling them to disseminate this sutra.
Through the expedient means of reciting, copying, and transcribing [the scriptures], they provide rescue and relief,
ensuring that beings do not encounter evil and always practice a virtuous mind.
At that time, the Gandharva kings and their respective retinues prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and reverently practiced his teachings with single-minded devotion.
The Buddha then addressed Ānanda:
I stroke the crown of your head with my right hand.
You must apply yourself with diligence;
this sutra is the sole charge I entrust to you.
Ānanda, you must diligently propagate this sutra so that all sentient beings may hear and know it.
Ānanda, you are truly the foremost disciple within my heart.
I entrust all the dharmas I have brought forth to you.
Out of my compassion for all sentient beings and my desire to bring them to liberation, I do this now.
The Buddha returned to his proper seat and entrusted this Dharma to him, saying:
"Ānanda, this sutra is most venerable and formidable, possessing supreme majestic power.
I exhort all men and women of good family to make offerings of incense, flowers, and various colored silks, and to light lamps to maintain the illumination."
Furthermore, those who are able to circulate, read,
and recite it shall all be delivered from the miseries and calamities of illness;
they will enjoy peace and prosperity in this present life.
In the future, when they are reborn in the Land of Immeasurable Life, they will immediately be born within lotus flowers with golden-hued bodies and complete physical marks;
their wisdom and vigor shall be equal to those of the highest grade.
The merit is thus beyond measure or calculation.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"One should use fine paper, fine brushes, and fine ink."
With a sincere heart, transcribe the Dharma I have spoken,
with every line and verse exactly as the Buddha taught it;
do not allow even a single stroke or a single dot to be lost through negligence.
Ānanda, out of my compassion for sentient beings,
I entrust this Dharma solely to you,
so that all classes of living beings may hear and know it.
With his mind opened and his understanding resolved, he constantly practiced wholesome dharmas.
At that time, Ānanda stood before the World-Honored One with palms joined in single-minded devotion;
the hairs on his body all stood on end, and he trembled with awe.
With single-minded attention, they listened to the Buddha’s words, not daring to forget even a single sentence or verse.
Shedding tears, they said,
"We shall wholeheartedly receive and uphold that which the World-Honored One has entrusted to us."
"May you cause this sutra to be widely circulated.
Ānanda spoke again:
"I shall receive the teaching of the World-Honored One."
Prostrating at the Buddha’s feet, they single-mindedly practiced his teachings.
Cultivating merit, they received the retribution of happiness; whatever they desired arose spontaneously.
They transcended the stream of birth and death and attained the ultimate state of Nirvana.

If a person delights in performing merit, the celestial deities will naturally protect them, and all their aspirations will spontaneously be fulfilled; the various Māras shall be unable to destroy them.
One with little merit encounters many afflictions, whereas merit can eliminate all calamities.
When merit is firm and strong, one swiftly achieves steadfastness and is born in heaven to experience joy;
even among humans one possesses sovereignty,
all because of these merits, such that wherever one goes, everything is spontaneous.
Therefore, through these skillful means of merit, one is forever freed from the suffering of birth and death,
attains nirvāṇa, and neither perishes nor is born again.
*The Scripture on Saving and Protecting One’s Body and Life*, one fascicle.
